hash_policy: Record a checksum only for source bytes actually obtained; no source bytes or invented hashes are recorded by this planning inventory.

pinpoints: Mandatory requirements: Patient safety alerts and notifications
supports: For applicable SAC1 incidents, reporting through RiskMan within one business day of awareness and analysis/report submission within 90 calendar days of reporting as SAC1.
Analysis reports contain event facts, contributing factors and recommendations addressing recurrence.
Locally identified patient safety issues with potential statewide impact are reported through the authorised process.
limitations: This record references the existing canonical source; it neither replaces its metadata nor creates a second rules registry.
The directive does not make every death or incident a SAC1 event.
Correct applicability, distinct trigger dates and authorised submission remain necessary; generating a report does not prove submission.
No new deadline rule or operational connector is enabled by this track inventory.

authority_source_references.observed_revision: Version history 4.0 dated 13 March 2026; page last updated 18 June 2026
pinpoints: 3.2.2-3.2.4: method selection and statutory RCA conditions
supports: Queensland Health does not prescribe one analysis method for SAC1 incidents.
Patient, family and carer perspectives and consumer representation inform the analysis and recommendations.
Accessible reports distinguish factual descriptions, contributing factors and recommendations.
Recommendations should identify responsible people, timescales, monitoring, expected outcomes and measures of impact and sustainability.
Statutory RCA protection has conditions distinct from the review method label; reportable-event status is a stated necessary condition.

metadata_conflict.disposition: Preserve the conflict and canonical registry record; do not infer withdrawal or silently correct the issuer's dates.

limitations: Guidance expressed as should is not converted into a mandatory rule without a separate applicable authority.
The public guideline does not establish the exact current HEAPS template fields or CHHHS local workflow.
A reportable event is not by itself proof that statutory RCA protection applies; authorised case-specific governance remains separate.
No source-text interpretation or method selector grants clinical, legal, disclosure or organisational authority.

supplementary_sources.title: Incident review templates
supplementary_sources.issuer: Queensland Health Safety and Quality Education Program
supports: An official public resource index points to HEAPS tools and morbidity and mortality review templates on QHEPS.
limitations: The linked HEAPS tools were not retrieved and no intranet authentication was attempted.
Exact current fields, sections, mandatory rules, factor taxonomy, local adaptations and redistribution rights remain unknown.
The landing-page update date is not a verified template revision.

supplementary_sources.title: Best practice guide to clinical incident management
supplementary_sources.retrieval_detail: The initial web retrieval returned indexed PDF text with 126 pages and 7041 total lines reported, but displayed only lines 0-544 covering the title, licence, contents and introductory material. A separate search excerpt exposed printed page 42. Subsequent live open/find/screenshot requests returned 404 or inaccessible responses. No complete PDF bytes were obtained.
pinpoints: Printed page 2: publication and licence statement, initial indexed text
Printed pages 3-5: contents, initial indexed text
Printed page 42: analysis-method description, indexed search excerpt only
supports: The observed edition identifies HEAPS, RCA and London Protocol as tools available for comprehensive analysis.
The guide contents distinguish general incident-management stages including preparation, analysis, follow-through and closing the loop.
limitations: The /2018-01/ URL path is not the document edition; the inspected title identifies January 2023.
The page 42 passage was indexed text, not a successfully retrieved current PDF page.
The general six incident-management stages do not establish an authenticated six-step HEAPS template.
No complete current-content, current-link or template-fidelity claim is admitted from this partial observation.
supplementary_sources.rights_handling: Initial indexed page 2 states Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia for the guide; this inventory links and paraphrases only. No template, logo or third-party-material rights are inferred.

supplementary_sources.title: Patient Safety: From Learning to Action III
pinpoints: Printed page 1: publication and reproduction conditions
Printed page 14: HEAPS contributing-factor domains and analysis boundaries
supports: Historical HEAPS domains include patient, task, practitioner, team, workplace and organisational factors.
The historical account describes staff training and system learning alongside, rather than replacing, separate accountability processes.
limitations: This report concerns 2007-08 practice and superseded incident-management arrangements.
Historical descriptions do not set current SAC eligibility, mandated method selection, deadlines or team membership.
The six factor domains are not six process steps and are not a verified current official template taxonomy.
supplementary_sources.rights_handling: links_and_original_mapping_only; no report or template copy redistributed

supplementary_sources.title: Independent Governance Review: Metro North Hospital and Health Services - Caboolture Hospital - Surgery
supplementary_sources.issuer: Independent review published by Metro North Health
supports: The review recommends independent re-review, explicit timeline sections and links between contributing factors and recommendations in HEAPS and RCA reports.
It recommends checking duplicated prior recommendations and governance review before finalisation.
limitations: These are recommendations from a particular 2021 review, not a current statewide HEAPS mandate or proof of CHHHS policy.
Proposed rcagent quality checks draw on these failure modes but do not claim that agents supply independent clinical review.
supplementary_sources.rights_handling: links_and_original_mapping_only; no report or official template copied

supplementary_sources.title: Health service entity's management and reporting of clinical incidents - snapshot report
supplementary_sources.issuer: Office of the Health Ombudsman, Queensland
pinpoints: Page 2: evidence gaps in action-plan and improvement follow-through
supports: Review recurring themes and implementation progress; date action plans and identify responsible people and ongoing or completed actions.
The evaluated entity had gaps in evidence connecting audit findings to implemented corrective actions.
limitations: The report evaluates one entity; it does not establish the performance of CHHHS or every HEAPS review.
Implementation progress is not proof of effectiveness, and this source is not a HEAPS field-level specification.

scope: Current CHHHS clinical incident management procedure and applicable HEAPS review template
Relevant statewide HEAPS tool revision and any documented local adaptation
required_provenance: Document identifier, title, version, approval/effective/review dates and current-status confirmation
Relationship to the statewide instrument and scope of local applicability
Source location, access date, access classification and authorised environment
Permission to inspect, adapt and redistribute recorded separately
Checksum of actual obtained bytes if an authorised copy is acquired
local_source_intake.content_boundary: Blank documents only, without patient, staff, case or incident identifiers, credentials, completed reviews or internal comments. Blank does not itself mean public or redistributable.
local_source_intake.public_repository_admission: Keep restricted source bytes in the authorised environment. Admit only a rights-cleared original field crosswalk and synthetic examples to the public repository; do not copy official wording, branding or templates by default.
field_crosswalk: Required, optional or conditional status with exact source basis
Canonical rcagent object and provenance mapping
Local role, approval or escalation dependency
Conflict, ambiguity, missing evidence and disposition
dependent_claims_held: Local clinical, legal, records, disclosure or deployment approval
local_source_intake.independent_work_permitted: Public-source planning, original contracts, synthetic fixtures and non-operational quality checks may proceed without implying that the local-source gaps are resolved.
